pull_request.title: Infrastructure: Synchronize remaining device token accounting
pull_request.head: infrastructure/device-accounting-sync-20261012
pull_request.body:
## Change

Recover token usage retained on this device and synchronize it with the token dashboard merged in #63. Add **26 disjoint closed turns: 67,616,498 input + 258,998 output = 67,875,496 tokens**, including the completed audit and publication turns. The observed project subtotal is **620,812,827 tokens across 209 dated turns**; cached input and reasoning output remain subsets.

Restore eight original publication journal pairs from exact local branch revision `7ec9d05dc5ee9aefdf6c0da30549615ebc06a0b0`, preserving their provenance and appending dated accounting corrections. Usage-only inventories retain verified request arithmetic, exact boundaries, event hashes and one canonical owner per turn. Three PubDoc child turns reconcile independently; shared multi-PR turns are counted once. All 183 observations and canonical owners on main, including #61's calorimeter attribution, are preserved.

Merge current main (`2534ae86e89a10894ed3e7c47f3a83d451774de6`) with ordinary Git history. Although the textual merge is clean, the new token collector initially rejected a September 25 provisional snapshot when compared with its later final counters. Recognize explicitly in-progress, unclosed snapshots without completion boundaries as lower-bound evidence. They supply neither final counters nor dates, and cannot exceed known final counters. Finalized-counter/date conflicts and duplicate ownership still fail. Historical inventory files remain byte-identical; two new regression tests cover this case.

Coverage remains partial: one token-gate turn (1,773,512 tokens) is retained pending reconciliation with excluded, pre-existing untracked work; 13 historical turns remain unassigned, four failed turns lack observations, and the current compatibility-check turn remains active. No estimates or scientific approval are introduced. Governing workflow: ADR-004, unchanged.

## Dashboard and validation

- [x] Infrastructure accounting/collector correction; no scientific progress entries added.
- [x] **71 Python tests pass:** 10 token-site, 22 logger, 11 recovery and 28 project-record tests.
- [x] Session validation/summary, current project validation, token-site validation/build and whitespace checks pass.
- [x] All prior inventories and observations, scientific registers and four unrelated untracked files verified preserved.
- [x] Human approval boundaries preserved; ordinary merge and push retain shared history.

Node is unavailable locally; the unchanged JavaScript interaction check runs in hosted CI. The old dashboard CI success predates #63; the updated branch requests the current workflows.

Evidence: `logs/codex/SESSION-2026-10-12-device-accounting-audit.md`, `SESSION-2026-10-12-device-accounting-pr.md` and `SESSION-2026-10-12-pr62-main-sync.md`.

The user asked whether PR62 needs rebasing after PR63 merged. Started from
PR62 head `229e02aaddfe450af695dc221c624d7eaaf529c7` on
`infrastructure/device-accounting-sync-20261012`; the four unrelated untracked
token-gate files remain untouched. PR63 merged into main as
`2534ae86e89a10894ed3e7c47f3a83d451774de6`, including the PR61 calorimeter
ownership correction. GitHub showed PR62 as mergeable with passing old-dashboard
CI, but that did not validate the newly introduced token-site workflow.

Read the changed repository instructions and current token/project validation
guides. An ordinary merge in an isolated checkout was conflict-free but the new
token collector failed against the combined records. The branch therefore needs
a compatibility correction, despite having no textual merge conflict. The
repository requires ordinary merges, so shared history is preserved.
